title_en: Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Comprehensively Promoting the Construction of Litigation Service Centers of People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Comprehensively Promoting the Construction of People's Court Litigation Service Centers

Fa Fa [2014] No. 23

To thoroughly implement the principles of the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and the Third and Fourth Plenary Sessions of the 18th Central Committee, consolidate the achievements of the Party's mass line education and practice activities, firmly grasp the main line of judicial为民 and impartial justice, further improve judicial convenience and benefit measures for the people, effectively enhance the ability and level of judicial services to the masses, and strive to achieve the goal of enabling the people to feel fairness and justice in every judicial case, the following opinions are hereby put forward on comprehensively promoting the construction of People's Court litigation service centers:

I. Overall Goals and Basic Principles

1. By building litigation service halls, litigation service websites, and the 12368 litigation service hotline, construct a multi-channel, one-stop, comprehensive litigation service center for the People's Court facing society, facilitating parties to conveniently handle other litigation matters besides court trials with respect, build an open, dynamic, transparent, and convenient sunshine judicial mechanism, deepen judicial openness, expand judicial democracy, strive to achieve judicial为民 and impartial justice, and enhance judicial credibility.

2. The litigation service center is an external service platform built for various departments of the court. Each department undertakes litigation service work according to its own functions and the overall operational requirements of the litigation service center, maximizing convenience for the masses in litigation.

3. The construction of the litigation service center adheres to the principle of "facing the masses, facing the grassroots, facing reality." The functional settings, service procedures, and service standards shall be determined based on the actual needs of facilitating parties in exercising their litigation rights and ensuring the people's right to know and supervise. Focus on the construction of grassroots People's Court litigation service centers, and attach great importance to improving the litigation service level of People's Tribunals. Pay attention to regional differences and level differences, proceed from reality, adapt measures to local conditions, and promote the construction of litigation service centers step by step. Focus on leveraging modern information technologies such as big data and cloud computing to actively expand service functions, enrich service content, and innovate service methods.

II. Litigation Service Hall

(A) Infrastructure

1. The litigation service hall shall have obvious signs to facilitate the entry and exit of the masses, and be equipped with barrier-free passages; the area shall meet the actual needs for function performance.

2. The reception area for petitions and other litigation service areas shall be set up separately, achieving a reasonable layout, dignified, spacious, bright, clean, and hygienic; on the premise of ensuring safety and order, open office modes such as "counter-style" and "window-style" shall be adopted; based on conditions and actual needs, green channels can be opened for disadvantaged groups such as the disabled to provide priority services. Establish a remote video petition reception system to achieve interconnection and intercommunication with higher and lower courts.

3. Provide rest seats, drinking water facilities, and sanitation service facilities; provide writing materials, paper, photocopying, typing, telephone, fax, internet, and other services; where conditions permit, provide other commodity services related to litigation.

4. Provide litigation guidance materials such as visitor instructions, litigation guides, and risk disclosure notices for the parties; equip with electronic touch screens and other self-service inquiry devices.

5. Post work processes, management systems, and relevant information of court and hall staff in conspicuous locations.

6. Equip with handheld security inspection devices, liquid detectors, channel-type X-ray baggage inspection machines, and explosion-proof barrels, fire blankets, and other security inspection equipment.

(B) Main Functions

1. Litigation Guidance and Legal Publicity. Assign dedicated personnel to receive visitors, guide them to relevant areas based on their purposes, and provide necessary litigation guidance and legal publicity.

2. Registration and Case Filing, Pre-litigation Mediation. Receive case materials, handle registration and case filing procedures, calculate litigation fees; provide parties, agents, and defenders with verification passwords for inquiring case information and accessing case files; provide judicial assistance to eligible parties, and handle reduction, deferment, or exemption of litigation fees according to regulations. If truly necessary, provide door-to-door case filing and holiday appointment case filing services. Where conditions permit, set up on-site financial institution service windows to achieve on-site payment of litigation fees and other expenses.

Set up mediation rooms, where judges and full-time people's mediators conduct pre-litigation mediation or case-filing mediation, and carry out litigation-mediation connection work.

3. Accept Applications, Transfer Materials. Accept applications from parties for property preservation, evidence preservation, entrustment of appraisal, etc., conduct a formal review, and then transfer to relevant departments for processing. Under special circumstances, provide services for urgently handling application matters.

Accept litigation materials submitted by parties, agents, and defenders, and transfer them to judges or collegial panels.

4. Inquiry and Consultation, Contacting Judges. Through window reception, touch screens, the internet, and other means and forms, provide parties, agents, and defenders with case information inquiry services such as the presiding judge, trial organization, and case progress information. Provide legal consultation to parties; where conditions permit, provide psychological counseling related to litigation. Provide dedicated case reading rooms to facilitate parties, agents, and defenders in accessing case files according to regulations, and provide scanning, photocopying, and other services. If parties, agents, or defenders need to contact a judge, promptly assist in contacting; if there is a legitimate reason and the judge agrees, arrange a meeting with the judge at a designated location.

Based on conditions and actual needs, set up lawyer or volunteer service windows, where lawyers or volunteers with professional knowledge provide free litigation consultation and assistance to the parties. Actively strive to include the free services of lawyers in the litigation service hall within the scope of legal aid.

5. Document Service and Post-Judgment Responses. After the collegial panel has agreed with the party, provide window service for serving litigation documents to the party. If a party raises questions about the judgment, notify the collegial panel to respond.

6. Petition Reception, Complaints and Suggestions. Receive and handle appeals and petitions; conduct remote video petition reception.

Set up complaint mailboxes, accept reports, complaints, opinions, and suggestions, and transfer them to relevant departments for processing. Where conditions permit, set up disciplinary inspection windows.

(C) Position Requirements

1. Guidance personnel may be non-trial personnel; they shall use civilized and standardized language to inquire about the visitor's purpose, introduce procedures, direct to the location, and conduct legal publicity.

2. When the case-filing judge finds that the civil dispute initiated by the party is suitable for mediation and obtains the party's consent, the judge shall promptly transfer the case to mediation. For cases that do not meet the mediation conditions, inform the party of litigation risks and promptly handle registration and case filing procedures. If the materials are incomplete, guide the party to complete them at one time; if the case cannot be filed immediately, explain the reasons and agree on a case-filing time; if the conditions for registration and case filing are not met, provide legal clarification and guidance.

Pre-litigation mediators shall conduct mediation based on the principles of legality and voluntariness. If the party is unwilling to mediate or fails to reach a mediation agreement, promptly transfer to case-filing and trial procedures.

3. The position for accepting applications shall be staffed by judges or judge assistants rotated from the civil, administrative trial departments and the enforcement department. Standardize the form requirements for common applications. Issue a receipt upon receiving application materials, conduct a careful review; if the materials are incomplete, guide the party to complete them at one time; if they meet formal requirements, promptly transfer to the relevant department for processing.

4. The positions for material transfer, inquiry and consultation, and contacting judges may be held by non-trial personnel. When transferring materials, carefully check, register, issue a receipt, and ensure timely handover. Verify the inquirer's identity, promptly assist with inquiries, or guide them to use self-service inquiry devices. Carefully listen to visitors' questions, answer patiently, explain legal provisions in detail, and provide litigation guidance.

5. The position for window document service may be held by non-trial personnel. Service of documents shall be carried out strictly in accordance with legal provisions. If a party raises questions about the judgment document on the spot, immediately notify the collegial panel to respond, or have the collegial panel schedule a time with the party to respond.

6. Petition reception judges shall promptly receive visitors, carefully review petition materials, listen to opinions, and fully record visitor information. If they can respond on the spot, do so; if not, handle within the prescribed time limit. For abnormal petitions such as collective petitions, report promptly and handle appropriately to prevent intensification of conflicts.

7. If a disciplinary inspection window is established, the position for complaints and suggestions shall be staffed by personnel from the disciplinary inspection department; if not established, it may be held by other non-trial personnel. Promptly handle and transfer reports and complaints according to relevant regulations, and strictly observe confidentiality discipline; periodically summarize opinions and suggestions for transfer to relevant departments.

8. Security personnel shall be judicial police; they shall strictly guard their posts, enforce the law in a civilized manner, diligently perform security inspection duties, and ensure site safety and order.

III. Litigation Service Website

(A) Infrastructure

1. Establish a litigation service website, improve databases such as court public information, case process information, and litigation electronic archives as support for the litigation service website. Achieve mutual linking and resource sharing between the litigation service website and the trial process disclosure platform, judgment document disclosure platform, and enforcement information disclosure platform (the three major judicial disclosure platforms).

2. Establish a communication service system to achieve information sharing and interconnection with the litigation service hall, litigation service website, and 12368 litigation service hotline.

3. Improve the case process management system and online office system to achieve timely data exchange with the litigation service website and communication service system.

(B) Main Functions

1. Information Inquiry, Litigation Guidance. From the date of case acceptance, parties, agents, and defenders can log in to the webpage using an inquiry password to inquire about case information. The public can directly log in to the webpage to inquire about public information such as court institutions, personnel, work processes, effective judgment documents, commonly used laws and regulations, and litigation guidance information. Provide electronic documents of commonly used formats such as complaints, defenses, enforcement applications, and powers of attorney for parties to view and download. Through the communication service system, actively push main case process node information to parties, agents, and defenders via SMS, WeChat, Weibo, mobile communication application clients, etc., or push relevant case information based on inquiry applications, and actively push public information to the public.

2. Appointment Case Filing, Online Case Filing. Parties submit case materials online, and after online review by the case-filing judge, if conditions for registration and case filing are met, schedule an appointment for the party or agent to go to the litigation service hall to complete the case filing procedures.

Explore the establishment of a mechanism for verifying the authenticity of litigation acts to achieve online registration and case filing by the case-filing judge. Explore the establishment of an online payment system to provide parties with online payment services for litigation fees and other expenses.

3. Accept Applications, Receive Materials. Parties submit applications for property preservation, evidence preservation, entrustment of appraisal, etc. online; the judge reviews online; if formal requirements are met, schedule an appointment for the applicant to submit a written application at the litigation service hall. Explore the establishment of a mechanism for verifying the authenticity of litigation acts to achieve online review and processing of relevant applications by the judge.

Parties, agents, and defenders upload case materials online, and the judge responds after processing.

4. Contacting Judges, Online Case Review. On the basis of electronic litigation archives, provide online case review services. After password verification, parties, agents, and defenders can review case files online or download them in accordance with relevant regulations.

Parties, agents, and defenders can request to speak with a judge, meet a judge, or leave a message for a judge on a specific case public communication platform via the internet; the judge responds after processing.

5. Online Petition, Appointment Reception. Parties upload petition materials and submit petition requests; the petition judge handles the matter online through the online petition system and replies to the party. Parties apply online for appointment reception; the petition judge reviews and schedules.

(C) Position Requirements

1. The litigation service website shall be managed and maintained by specialized institutions and personnel to ensure normal operation; relevant departments shall be responsible for updating public information in a timely manner; judges and auxiliary personnel shall promptly input case information to ensure effective functioning of information inquiry and litigation guidance functions.

2. The online case-filing judge shall carefully review the case materials submitted by the party; if conditions for registration and case filing are met, promptly notify the party or agent to go to the litigation service hall to complete the case filing procedures or directly decide to file the case. If the submitted materials are incomplete, guide the party to complete them online at one time. If conditions for registration and case filing are not met, reply with legal clarification and guidance.

3. The judge's personal terminal in the online office system is part of the litigation service website. Applications and materials submitted by parties, etc., reach the judge's personal terminal via data exchange; the presiding judge shall process and reply within the prescribed time.

4. The online petition judge shall carefully review the petition materials submitted by the petitioner, handle the matter within the prescribed time, fully fill in the handling opinions and reasons, and reply to the party online.

IV. 12368 Litigation Service Hotline

(A) Infrastructure

1. Open the 12368 litigation service hotline, set up a dedicated reception area, equip with necessary work facilities, achieve effective integration with the case process management system, online office system, litigation service website, and communication service system, and share the basic database.

2. Where conditions permit, achieve information voice activation and establish an automatic voice response system.

(B) Main Functions

1. Information Inquiry. From the date of case acceptance, parties, agents, and defenders can call the hotline to inquire about case information via automatic voice; if an automatic voice response system has not been established, the agent will answer the call, inquire, and reply, or push the inquiry result through the communication service system.

2. Litigation Consultation. Provide consultation on common procedural legal issues.

3. Contacting Judges. If parties, agents, or defenders call the hotline to request contact with a judge, assist in contacting.

4. Appointment Services. Based on conditions and actual needs, provide assistance in scheduling holiday case filing, door-to-door case filing, and other services.

(C) Position Requirements

1. Agents may be non-trial personnel, responsible for answering the hotline, recording, replying to related matters, and transferring. Ensure the hotline is open during business hours, listen patiently to callers, and make records. For inquiries and consultations, provide comprehensive and accurate answers; if a request to contact a judge is made, promptly assist in contacting; if contact cannot be made promptly, leave a message for the judge to reply to the caller within the prescribed time. Accurately record reports, complaints, opinions, and suggestions, promptly transfer them according to relevant regulations, and strictly observe confidentiality discipline.

2. The service hotline shall have dedicated management and maintenance personnel; if an automatic voice response system has been established, ensure it operates normally 24 hours a day.

V. System Construction

People's Courts at all levels shall, based on the functions of the litigation service hall, litigation service website, and 12368 litigation service hotline, formulate work rules, standardize operating procedures, strengthen mutual coordination, and ensure the standardized and efficient operation of the three major litigation service platforms. The following systems shall be established as a priority:

1. Standardized Service System. The three major litigation service platforms shall clearly define the processing time, deadlines, and requirements for each service item, and strictly implement them to ensure standardization of litigation services.

2. Position Responsibility System. For each position on the three major litigation service platforms, fixed post, fixed person, and fixed responsibility shall be implemented, achieving clear functions, clear tasks, and consistent rights and responsibilities. The first staff member to receive a visitor or answer a call is the first responsible person, who shall conscientiously and responsibly handle visitor reception, call answering, and registration. For matters within their scope of duties, handle promptly; for matters outside their scope, promptly transfer to relevant departments and personnel, and report the transfer situation to the visitor or caller in a timely manner.

Establish a scientific assessment mechanism to conduct separate assessments of the staff of the litigation service center.

3. Open Service System. The process and results of each litigation service work shall be recorded and convenient for the masses to understand and inquire, and shall be subject to public supervision. The three major litigation service platforms shall all establish a public satisfaction evaluation system.

4. Duty Judge System. Trial business departments shall arrange responsible leaders to be on duty at the litigation service center in rotation to guide the handling of difficult matters and coordinate the work of various departments.

5. Supervision and Reminder System. Judges and other staff shall complete relevant litigation service work within the prescribed time. If not completed within the prescribed time, the trial management system shall, in a certain manner, prompt their superior managers level by level for supervision.

6. Civilized Reception System. Staff of the litigation service center shall wear uniforms on duty, be energetic, dignified in appearance, proper in conduct, thoughtful in service, civil in language, efficient in work, and appropriate in methods.

VI. Work Requirements

1. Strengthen Organizational Leadership. People's Courts at all levels shall attach great importance to the construction of litigation service centers, insist on the president personally grasping the work, and coordinate the cooperation of all departments. Based on the overall requirements of the Supreme People's Court and local basic conditions and actual needs, formulate specific work plans, clarify the construction schedule, and actively implement them.

2. Unify the Name. The litigation service venues of People's Courts shall uniformly use the name "Litigation Service Center."

3. Strengthen Institutional Construction. People's Courts at all levels may rely on the case-filing division or build a daily management department for the litigation service center based on their actual circumstances. Pay attention to enhancing coordination; major matters shall be studied and handled by the responsible leader convening a coordination meeting attended by various departments to ensure efficient work.

4. Strengthen Team Building. In accordance with the requirements of "politically firm, professionally proficient, strictly disciplined, excellent in style, and noble in character," equip the litigation service center with adequate and strong staff. Strengthen professional training, implement regular job rotation; newly appointed judges and personnel to be appointed as intermediate leaders shall receive training at the litigation service center, making the center a base for cultivating and training cadres. Personnel may be classified and allocated according to different positions. Non-trial positions may be held by retired judges or volunteers, and labor outsourcing may be explored.

5. Pay Attention to Publicity. People's Courts at all levels shall make full use of various social media and the court's own media to increase publicity on the construction of litigation service centers, enhance the understanding of the masses, and strive for broad support from all sectors of society for the construction work.

6. Strengthen Supervision and Assessment. Higher People's Courts shall strengthen measures, strengthen the assessment and acceptance of the construction of litigation service centers by lower courts, and promote the continuous deepening of the construction work.

December 15, 2014
